summary:
All 89 Maths leaves (P1.1–P10.5, S1.1–S5.3, M6.1–M9.1) have notes, flashcards, a quiz and exam items. No leaf is missing. All 38,310 $…$ maths segments render in KaTeX 0.16.11 without an error. The shipped M7.3 is not bare: it has 8 note pages, about 1,770 words, 15 worked examples, 4 figures, 21 flashcards, 13 quiz items and 15 exam items, and all of it renders on the Mac and the iPhone. Two things can still make it look bare. First, its Specification tab is mangled PDF-extraction text. Second, if the user forked M7.3 before the Mechanics rewrite (4d791ca), that fork still hides the new notes, and no notice says so (edits.js does not check whether a fork is out of date). The most important root causes:
(1) The generated spec spine js/data/maths.js holds garbled text from PDF extraction. At least 36 of the 89 leaves have broken fragments, and 25 still contain "need to learn:".
(2) The quiz never shuffles its options, and the authored answers sit at A or B 95% of the time. Of 498 base items, 380 have the answer at A; of 560 bank items, 381 have it at B.
(3) The bank-*.js files were added on top of the base files without a duplicate check. That gives 17 exact repeats and about 45 groups of cards with the same answer inside one leaf.
(4) The gen_data.py SHORT_S table never reached the stats/mech titles, so every S and M leaf is titled with an 80-character spec sentence cut off with "…".
(5) Depth is very uneven. The thinnest base notes are 8.4 (~200 words), 8.1 (~260) and 6.1 (~330), against 8,667 words for 4.1. The core skills leaves 7.2, 8.2, 6.3 and 8.6 are each a few hundred words.
(6) The worked card's "Write it out" chip is absolutely positioned and overlaps the card title on every device, and it is only 23px tall.
coverage:
Content: I loaded every Maths content file and both banks in Node, in index.html's load order (script /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/cm/load.js). I measured every leaf: pages, blocks, words, worked and exam-tagged worked examples, figures, callouts, long paragraphs, flashcards, quiz items, exam items (base, bank and derived), and the position of the quiz answer (cm/metrics.js → cm/metrics.json).
Near-duplicate detection used two methods: token Jaccard (cm/dups.js) and canonical-LaTeX character 3-grams plus same-answer groups (cm/dups2.js → cm/dups2.json). I checked quiz structure and formatting (odd $ or **, LaTeX outside $, long answers). All maths segments were validated in KaTeX in the browser. I dumped and read every leaf's spec spine (cm/spine.txt).
Correctness: I hand-checked about 150 flashcards and quiz items in M7.3, 6.1, 8.1, M8.3, 5.2, S4.3, 9.3, S2.3, M8.6, 4.3 and 10.4, recomputing the numbers. I found one wrong answer.
Visual: M7.3 Notes, Spec and the past-paper page on Mac (Graphite); M7.3 Notes pages 1 and 6 on iPhone; the M7.3 quiz on iPad portrait (Dawn); 8.4 Notes full page on Mac; 5.6 Spec on Mac; M7.2 Notes figure on Mac in Dawn. I measured the Write-it-out geometry at mac, ipad, ipadl and iphone.
Not examined: I did not hand-verify every numeric answer in all 1,058 quiz items and 1,500+ flashcards; there was no automated maths checker. I did not read exam-item mark schemes beyond the derivation code. I did not test a shop theme or the seeded account; Maths content does not depend on account data apart from forks. I could not see the user's own state.edits, so the fork theory for "M7.3 is bare" is inferred from code and git history, not observed.

findings.title: Specification tab shows garbled PDF-extraction text on most Maths leaves (M7.3 included)
findings.detail: The Spec tab is drawn from js/data/maths.js content/info lines, which are raw, broken PDF extraction. Examples: M7.3 guidance reads "v = u + at r = ut +1at2 / e.g. , with vectors / 2 given in i - j or column vector form". 5.6 reads "Understand and use double a n g le f / rm u l a e ; u s e / f s in ( A ± B ), fo r m u l a e fo r / ± ± cos (A B)". 2.1 reads "× = , ÷ = - , = m n n am / The equivalence ofa and should be known." 2.10 starts mid-sentence: "into partial fractions". 25 leaves still contain the extraction artefact "need to learn:" or "students need to learn:". A heuristic found fragment lines in 36 of the 89 leaves: 1.1 2.1 2.2 2.3 2.4 2.5 2.7 2.9 3.3 4.1 4.2 4.3 5.1 5.2 5.3 5.5 5.6 5.7 6.2 6.3 6.4 7.1 7.2 7.4 8.2 8.3 8.5 8.6 9.4 10.4 S2.3 S4.1 S5.3 M7.4 M8.3 M8.6, and reading the dump shows more. Exponents, fractions, sums and integrals are lost throughout. This is very likely part of why M7.3 looks bare.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-spec-mac.png; shots/content-maths/p5-6-spec-mac.png; cm/spine.txt (every leaf's spec text); tools/gen_data.py:240-255 (maths_group copies clean(x) of the extracted lines)
findings.fix: Hand-author the 89 Maths spec entries from the Edexcel 9MA0 PDF as typeset blocks (LaTeX in $…$). Either fix the extractor or add a checked-in override table that gen_data.py applies (as SHORT does), and regenerate. Drop the "need to learn:" headers. Add a smoke test that refuses fragment lines (≤4 characters, runs of single letters, "need to learn").
findings.rootCause: The spec spine is generated from a PDF text extraction (/home/claude/extract) that splits equations and kerned headings, and no override or cleanup pass exists for Maths.

findings.title: Quiz answers are almost always A or B, and options are never shuffled
findings.detail: Of 1,058 Maths quiz items, the correct option is A in 531 and B in 481. Only 44 are C and 2 are D. Base files: 380 A, 100 B, 17 C, 1 D. Bank files: 151 A, 381 B, 27 C, 1 D. KOS.quiz.mountMCQ renders opts in authored order, and its Shuffle button only reorders the questions. A learner soon learns to pick A on a base item or B on a bank item, so the quiz score stops measuring understanding. Separately, the correct option is uniquely the longest in 317 items (30%).
findings.evidence: cm/metrics.json ansDist per leaf; js/engines/quiz.js:66 (Shuffle shuffles order only), :88-96 (item.opts rendered in order, answer compared to item.ans at :113); e.g. js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js:305-306 (every item ans: 0); shots/content-maths/m73-quiz-ipad.png (Q1 answer A)
findings.fix: In mountMCQ, shuffle a per-question option permutation at mount and on Retry, seeded per attempt, and map clicks back to the original index so the stats and the why text stay valid. Optionally also rebalance the authored ans positions so a fixed order is fair too.
findings.rootCause: Authors put the right answer first (bank authors second), and the engine trusts the authored order.

findings.title: "Write it out" chip overlaps worked-example titles on every device and is only 23px tall
findings.detail: On worked cards with more than one step, the "Write it out" pill is position:absolute at the top-right, and the .k-n-worked-head row reserves no room for it. On M7.3's notes it lies over the title or src text on 4 of 15 cards on the Mac (1470), 2 of 15 on iPad portrait, 3 of 15 on iPad landscape and 9 of 15 on iPhone (402). Example on the Mac: "Write it out" is printed over "AS Specimen · P2 Q1(a)(b) · 5 marks". On iPhone it covers "Find the initial velocity". The pill measures 81×23 px with min-block-size:0, below the 44px touch minimum (invariant 69). The same overlap affects every subject's worked cards, because content.js is shared.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/writeout-overlap-mac.png; shots/content-maths/m73-notes-p6-iphone.png; measured: btn rect [233,618,81,23] while .k-n-worked-head starts at y=626, width 334 (iphone); css/views/ink.css:300; js/core/content.js:373; css/views/study.css:346
findings.fix: Put the chip in the head's flex flow (margin-inline-start:auto, before Copy) instead of absolute positioning, or give the head padding-inline-end equal to the chip's and Copy's widths. Raise the hit area to 44px for coarse pointers.
findings.rootCause: An absolutely positioned control added onto a flex header that wraps freely.

findings.title: A curriculum fork silently hides later curriculum upgrades (plausible cause of "M7.3 is basically bare")
findings.detail: KOS.content.get and srs read state.edits first (invariant 86). A fork copies the shipped material at the moment of the first edit and is never compared with the curriculum again. M7.3 was an outline entry until commit 4d791ca ("load M6–M7 at depth, drop their outline entries"), and a9f64b5 rewrote M7.2 and M7.3. A Notes fork made before then (or one carried over from S7.3 by the ref rename, router.js:117 renamedRef) keeps showing the old, thin outline notes. Nothing tells the user that a newer, much deeper version exists. The only sign is the Edit button's data-state forked (hub.js:2828). The shipped M7.3 renders in full (8 pages), so a bare M7.3 on the user's device most likely comes from such a fork.
findings.evidence: js/core/edits.js:1-60 (no base hash or staleness check: grep for stale/baseHash finds nothing); git log -- js/data/content/maths-mech-m7.js (a9f64b5, 4d791ca); shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (shipped content present)
findings.fix: Record a hash of the shipped kind on each fork (fork.base). When the shipped hash differs, show a banner on the tab: "The curriculum for this topic was updated after you edited it: View new · Keep mine · Merge (append your rows)". Check the user's real state for state.edits.topics['maths:M7.3'] (or 'maths:S7.3').
findings.rootCause: The fork model has no notion of the base version it was taken from.

findings.title: Bank files duplicate base flashcards and quiz items in the same leaf (17 exact repeats, about 45 same-answer groups)
findings.detail: bank-maths-*.js were added without a duplicate check against the base items. Exact repeats in the same quiz include: 2.1 "$8^{2/3}$ =" (qz0 and qz8); 4.1 "$\binom92$" (qz0 and qz18), "Coefficient of $x$ in $(2+x)^5$" (qz8 and qz22), "Coefficient of $x^2$ in $(1+x)(1+4x+6x^2)$" (qz10 and qz24), "$(1+3x)^{-1}$ valid for" (qz4 and qz20); 5.2 "$\sin3\theta\approx$" and "$1-\cos2\theta\approx$" both twice; 5.3 "$\tan\frac{3\pi}4$" twice; 5.6 "$\cos(A-B)$" twice; 6.3 "$\log_{10}0.001$" twice; 2.6 "$(x-2)$ is a factor means" twice; 2.8 "inverse only if one-to-one" twice; 7.2 "$d/dx\sqrt x$" twice. Flashcard and quiz pairs on the same fact: M7.3 "Which equation has no t?" (fc1 and qz10, and qz1 again); M7.5 time of flight and greatest height; 8.5 "∫ln x"; 7.5 "d/dx(3y²)"; 3.3 parametric dy/dx; 10.3 midpoint; 8.1 states the FTC twice (fc0 and fc5b) and uses the same f′ setup twice (fc4 and fc6b); 6.1 has "$e^{2x}=5$" as fc10b and qz3, "features of $a^x$" as fc0 and fc7b, and the asymptotes of $e^x+3$ and $e^x+2$ as qz0 and qz6b; 10.4 has "|AC| = 4 with one unknown" three times. Cross-leaf: S4.2 and S4.3 repeat continuity-correction cards, and S4.1 and S5.2 repeat "$P(X\ge k)$ in cumulative form". Full list: cm/dups2.json (66 within-leaf pairs, 14 cross-leaf pairs, 45 same-answer groups).
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/cm/dups2.json; e.g. js/data/content/maths-pure-p8.js:505 vs bank-maths-pure-c.js:457 ("Before integrating x²/(x−1) you should")
findings.fix: Delete or replace the bank items flagged in dups2.json with new item shapes. Add a smoke test that canonicalises q and the answer (\dfrac→\frac, strip spaces) and fails on an exact or same-answer duplicate inside one leaf. Removing flashcards must follow invariant 87 (carry the original index as a third element).
findings.rootCause: KOS.content.extend concatenates bank arrays blindly, and no test checks for duplicates.

findings.title: Thin notes on core Pure and Applied leaves (depth very uneven: 200 to 8,700 words)
findings.detail: Base notes (before the bank's past-paper page), as approximate words / pages / worked examples: 8.4 Integration as a limit of a sum 204/1/2; 8.1 Fundamental Theorem 258/1/2; 6.1 Exponential functions 331/2/2; 6.2 Gradient of e^kx 350/1/2 (no page breaks at all); 6.5 Solving a^x=b 401/2/4; 8.6 Integration with partial fractions 414/2/3; 4.3 Sigma 452/2/3; 4.6 Series in modelling 479/2/3 (no exam-tagged worked examples, so only 2 exam items); 7.2 Differentiating x^n, e^kx, trig, ln x 486/2/4; 6.3 Logarithms 489/2/4; M8.3 Weight 558/3/4 (3 exam items); 5.4 Reciprocal and inverse trig 563; S4.3 Selecting a distribution 587 (4 exam items); 8.8 617; 6.4 627; 3.4 632; 10.4 636/1/3; 8.2 Integrating standard functions 637; 9.5 773/1. The median leaf is about 1,040 words, and 4.1 has 8,667 words and 31 worked examples. 7.2 and 8.2 carry most of Paper 1 and 2 calculus but have the depth of a summary. Leaves with 5 or fewer exam items: 2.11 3.4 4.6 5.3 5.4 6.1 6.2 8.1 8.4 8.6 8.8 9.5 S4.3 M8.1 M8.3 M8.5.
findings.evidence: cm/metrics.json; table printed by cm/metrics.js; shots/content-maths/p8-4-notes-mac.png (8.4 is one short page)
findings.fix: Run the per-section depth pipeline used for 4.1, 2.x and M7 on P6 (6.1–6.5), P7.2, P8.1, 8.2, 8.4, 8.6, 8.8, 4.3, 4.6, 5.4, 10.4, 9.5, S4.3 and M8.3. Target at least 3 pages, at least 5 exam-tagged worked examples with Edexcel marks, a figure where a picture helps, and an exam toolkit page.
findings.rootCause: The depth rewrite stopped short on P6 to P8 and several small leaves. The files for P1, P9, P10 and M7 to M9 are dated 8 October and P2 to P8 27 October, and the light leaves were never brought up to the contract.

findings.title: Statistics and Mechanics leaf titles are cut-off 80-character spec sentences, unlike the short Pure titles
findings.detail: Pure leaves have names like "Straight lines" and "Trapezium rule". Every S and M leaf is titled with the first 80 characters of its spec sentence plus "…", e.g. M7.3 "Understand, use and derive the formulae for constant acceleration for motion in …" and S4.1 "simple, discrete probability distributions" (lowercase fragment). The page title is then cut again to three lines with an ellipsis, the spine rows read "Understand and use the lang…" five times in a row under M7, and the search results and breadcrumbs show the same. gen_data.py already defines SHORT_S ("suvat (constant acceleration)", "Projectiles", …), but it is never applied to the checked-in maths.js. Its keys are bare ("7.3") while the payload's refs are "S1.1" and "M7.3", and the generator cannot run locally (it reads /home/claude/extract).
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-mac.png (title and spine); shots/content-maths/m73-notes-iphone.png; tools/gen_data.py:249 (80-char truncation), :287-301 (SHORT_S and its lookup by c["ref"]); js/data/maths.js:989 ("S1.1"), :1287 ("M7.3")
findings.fix: Key SHORT_S by the final refs (S1.1…S5.3, M6.1…M9.1) and add a payload-only pass, like --mech-refs, that applies titles to the checked-in maths.js. Then regenerate.
findings.rootCause: The short-title table is keyed by refs that never match the stats and mech children, and the generator's source is not available to re-run.

findings.title: Wrong flashcard answer: 9.3 Newton–Raphson from x0 = 0 gives x1 = −2.5, not 2.5
findings.detail: 9.3 FC5 (bank) asks "Why does $x_0 = 0$ fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" and answers "it does not fail here; $x_1 = 2.5$". In fact f(0) = −5 and f′(0) = −2, so x1 = 0 − (−5)/(−2) = −2.5, which the card's own formula (2x³+5)/(3x²−2) also gives. The question also states something false: it says the method fails and the answer says it does not.
findings.fix: Rewrite the card, e.g. "Where would NR fail for $f(x)=x^3-2x-5$?" → "Where $f'(x_0)=0$: $x_0=\pm\sqrt{2/3}$". Or keep the x0 = 0 example with "$x_1=-2.5$ (far from the root 2.09)". Keep its schedule key (invariant 87).
findings.rootCause: An arithmetic sign slip in the bank author's answer, with no automated check on numeric answers.

findings.title: Cards filed under the wrong leaf
findings.detail: 6.1 (Exponential functions) holds solve-a^x=b items that belong to 6.5: fc3 "Solve $4^x=100$", fc10b "$e^{2x}=5$", fc13b "$2^x=20$", qz3. M8.3 (Weight and gravity) holds suvat projectile items that belong to M7.3: fc13b impact speed and fc14b rebound height. S4.3 (Selecting a distribution) holds normal-approximation and continuity-correction drill that belongs to S4.2: fc10b–fc14b, qz4b, qz5b, qz7b. 2.10 (Partial fractions) qz3 is an integral, ∫2/(x+1), which is 8.6's topic. 10.4 fc8b is an average-speed question. 8.1 fc9b ends without an answer ("a third condition is needed").
findings.evidence: cm/load.js dumps; read with the node print script (outputs quoted in this audit); bank-maths-pure-*.js, bank-maths-mech.js, bank-maths-stats.js
findings.fix: Move these items to their own leaves, keeping each card's original key as a whole-key third element (invariant 87), or replace them with items on the leaf's own skill.
findings.rootCause: Bank items were grouped by past-paper question rather than by spec point.

findings.title: "Past-paper patterns" pages are one wall-of-text paragraph
findings.detail: 55 of the 57 note paragraphs over 60 words sit on the bank's "Past-paper patterns" page. That is one per leaf, up to 135 words of run-on text with bold phrases and inline series lists. This goes against the user's rule of short lines and bullets, not paragraphs. On M7.3 page 8, one 6-line paragraph lists every question shape, and the lower half of the page is empty. It also repeats the M7.3 overview table of question shapes on page 1.
findings.evidence: shots/content-maths/m73-pastpaper-mac.png; js/data/content/bank-maths-*.js (each X(…) notes: [{page:"Past-paper patterns"}, "<long string>"]); counted by a script: 57 paragraphs over 60 words, 55 after the bank page
findings.fix: Convert each to a {table:{head:[Question shape, Marks, Seen in]}} or a {ul} of one shape per line, or fold it into the leaf's existing overview table and drop the page.
findings.rootCause: The bank files were written as prose summaries before the short-lines rule.

findings.title: 29 leaves have no figure where a picture would teach
findings.detail: Leaves with figs=0: 2.1 2.2 2.10 2.11 3.4 4.1 4.2 4.3 4.4 4.5 4.6 5.5 5.6 5.8 5.9 6.4 6.5 7.2 7.4 7.5 7.6 8.1 8.2 8.5 8.6 8.7 8.8 9.5 S3.3. Clear candidates: 5.9 Trig in context (Ferris wheel or tide curve), 5.6 R-form (the R·sin(θ+α) graph with max and min), 8.7 Separable DEs (family of solution curves, which the spec requires students to sketch), 3.4 Parametric modelling (motion path), 7.5 Implicit differentiation (circle with tangent), 4.2 Sequences (increasing, decreasing and periodic plots), 8.2 and 8.1 (antiderivative family), 2.11 modelling curves. Per the user's notes rule, annotated {fig} diagrams are expected wherever a picture helps.
findings.fix: Add declarative {fig} diagrams (core/figures.js) to these leaves during the depth pass. They are SVG-declarative, so no raster art is needed.
findings.rootCause: Figures were added only as each section was rewritten at depth.

findings.title: Units such as "m s$^{-1}$" break across lines
findings.detail: Units are authored as "m s$^{-1}$" with a normal space. At wrap points the line breaks inside the unit, leaving "…5 m s" at a line end and "−1" on the next line. Seen in M7.2's worked question in Dawn on the Mac ("travels at a constant 5 m s / −1 for the next 15 seconds").
findings.fix: Author units as a single KaTeX segment, e.g. $\text{m s}^{-1}$ or $5\ \text{m}\,\text{s}^{-1}$, or have inline() replace the space before a unit with U+00A0 and wrap the unit in a white-space:nowrap span.
findings.rootCause: A breakable space plus a separate math segment for the exponent.

findings.title: Two-option quiz items in a 4-option quiz
findings.detail: 8.1 qz9 ("$\int_2^5 f = -\int_5^2 f$ is: true / false") and 4.5 qz12 have only two options, so a guess is right 50% of the time, and they look different from the other items.
findings.evidence: cm/dups.json quizBad entries maths:8.1 #9 and maths:4.5 #12 (bank-maths-pure-c.js, bank-maths-pure-b.js)
findings.fix: Rewrite them as 4-option items, or as flashcards.
